seoTitle: Mount Kilimanjaro — Climbing Guide, Routes & Tips 2026
intro: Mount Kilimanjaro is Africa's highest peak at 5,895 metres (19,341 ft) and the world's tallest free-standing volcano. Located in the Kilimanjaro Region of northern Tanzania, it is one of the Seven Summits and the only one accessible to non-mountaineers — no ropes, crampons, or technical experience required. Around 50,000 climbers attempt Kilimanjaro annually with an overall summit success rate of 65–70%.

sections.heading: Routes to the Summit
sections.content: Six established routes reach Uhuru Peak. Marangu (5–6 days, huts): the most popular, sleeping in huts, ascending and descending the same path — success rates 85% on 6-day version. Machame (6–7 days, tents): the most scenic, follows a 'high camp' profile for better acclimatization. Lemosho (7–8 days, tents): the premium option — low traffic, best acclimatization, 90%+ success rate. Rongai (6 days): the only route approaching from the north, drier and less busy. Umbwe (5–6 days): the steepest and least recommended for acclimatization. Shira: merges with Lemosho after day 1.

sections.heading: Altitude Sickness — The Real Challenge
sections.content: Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) is the primary reason climbers fail to summit. Symptoms — headache, nausea, fatigue, dizziness — are normal above 3,000 metres and managed by the 'walk high, sleep low' principle built into longer routes. The medication Diamox (acetazolamide) reduces AMS symptoms; consult a doctor before use. Severe AMS (HACE/HAPE) requires immediate descent. The single most effective prevention is choosing a longer route with more acclimatization days — the difference between the 5-day and 7-day Lemosho summit rate is approximately 20 percentage points.

sections.heading: Cost and What's Included
sections.content: Tanzania requires all climbers to use a licensed operator. All-inclusive packages cover park fees ($700–900 for 6 days), licensed guide, assistant guides, porterage, cook, food, camping equipment, and airport transfers. Budget operators: $1,800–2,500. Mid-range: $2,500–3,500. Premium international: $4,000–6,000+. Tipping is a significant additional cost — $300–500 for a team of 8–10 on a 6-day climb is standard.

sections.heading: Best Time to Climb
sections.content: January–March: dry, clear skies, cold at summit, fewer crowds — excellent conditions. June–October: main dry season, warmest, highest foot traffic. Avoid April–May (long rains) and November (short rains) — trails are muddy and visibility poor. Summit temperature drops to -20°C on the coldest July nights; February is the warmest month at the summit (around -10°C).

faqs.q: How fit do I need to be to climb Kilimanjaro?
faqs.a: You need general cardiovascular fitness, not mountaineering ability. If you can hike 5–6 hours daily for several days at altitude, you have enough fitness. Altitude affects everyone regardless of fitness level — the key variable is acclimatization time, not fitness.

faqs.q: How long does it take to climb Kilimanjaro?
faqs.a: 5 to 9 days depending on route. The minimum recommended is 6 days (Marangu). Longer routes (7–8 days) have significantly higher summit success rates due to better acclimatization.

faqs.q: Can I climb Kilimanjaro without a guide?
faqs.a: No. Tanzania National Parks Authority (TANAPA) regulations require all climbers to be accompanied by a licensed guide. Independent climbing is not permitted on any route.

faqs.q: What gear do I need for Kilimanjaro?
faqs.a: Layering is critical: base layers (merino wool), mid-layer fleece, insulated jacket, waterproof shell, warm hat and gloves, gaiters, broken-in waterproof hiking boots, trekking poles, headlamp, sunscreen SPF 50+, UV sunglasses, and a hydration system (3–4 litres).

tips: Choose 6 days minimum — the extra day costs little but dramatically improves summit odds
Walk pole pole (slowly slowly) — rushing is the most common cause of failure
Break in your boots before the climb — blisters on day 1 ruin the entire experience
The summit push starts at midnight — sleep early on the day before summit night
Budget generously for porter tips — they carry 20kg so you can summit
